title: Schema Harmonization Runbook for Evidence Pipelines
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook captures a practical, minimally-invasive approach to harmonizing evidence and audit telemetry across our collectors, enrichment services, and SIEM export paths. Goal: produce a single canonical evidence schema and transformation rules that preserve security provenance (RBAC v2 context, request IDs, actor attributes), support efficient SIEM ingestion (Elastic/QRadar/Splunk), and minimize data duplication/cost when shipping logs and artifacts from Redwood-hosted and private deployments.

Context and motivation:
- We have many collector variants (edge harvester, sidecar, server-side ingest, ephemeral samplers). Each emits slightly different field names and encodings for the same semantic concepts (actor, resource, action, outcome, request_id, trace_id, k-v cache hit).
- Downstream: alerting rules and compliance audits rely on consistent field names and types. Manual mapping is brittle and expensive during incident/review.
- RBAC v2 introduces richer actor attributes: role_ids, role_sources, impersonation_chain. These must be preserved end-to-end for forensic timelines and queryability.

Non-goals:
- This runbook does not prescribe changes to all historical collectors. Aim is forward-compatible normalization and a migration strategy for older artifacts.

Canonical evidence schema (high-level):
We recommend a compact JSON object per event with the following canonical fields (all fields described as strings unless otherwise noted):
- event_type: (e.g., authz_check, api_call, infra_change, model_deploy)
- timestamp_iso8601: authoritative event time (UTC)
- request_id: unique per request across frontends/services
- trace_id: distributed trace id (if available)
- actor_id: opaque user/service id
- actor_identity: freeform display name or email
- actor_roles: comma-separated role ids (preserve RBAC v2 tokens)
- actor_role_sources: comma-separated role_source tags (e.g., okta, internal, impersonation)
- operation: a short verb (e.g., generate, upload, grant, revoke, read)
- resource: resource type + identifier (format: <type>:<id>)
- resource_namespace: e.g., customer-id or org-id
- outcome: success | failure | throttled | error
- outcome_code: machine code for outcome (map to SIEM severity later)
- reason: human-friendly explanation when outcome != success
- kvm_cache_hit: boolean (true/false as strings)
- evidence_refs: comma-separated URIs for associated artifacts (s3://, gs://, or internal blob ids)
- provenance: short provenance tag (ingest_sidecar, host_agent, server_ingest)
- shaped_payload: base64-encoded compact payload for indexed content when we need to keep token-limited fields (optional)

Field-level harmonization rules (transformer guidance):
- timestamp: prefer collector-provided authoritative timestamp. If absent, use ingest_time. Normalize to RFC3339 (truncate subseconds to micros).
- actor identity: collectors sometimes emit user_email vs username vs display_name. Normalizer should prefer email if present, else username, else "unknown_actor:<id>".
- roles: RBAC v2: flatten role array into actor_roles, preserving order if available. If a role object contains source and id, serialize as "<id>@<source>".
- impersonation_chain: append to actor_roles as a suffix if present with special separator "|impersonated:". Example: "role1@okta,role2@internal|impersonated:user:alice@example.com"
- resource: unifying: if collector emits separate fields (bucket, object_key), join into resource type:resource_id. Prefer stable ids over ephemeral paths.
- evidence_refs: normalize to canonical storage prefixes used by retention policy. If collector provides raw artifact payload, store to canonical object store and replace with ref.

Collector adapter patterns (implementation notes):
- Sidecar collector: lightweight prototypical normalizer implemented as a streaming transform (node/python) that consumes local protobuf/JSON and emits canonical events. Must be memory-bounded and backpressure-friendly.
- Server ingest pipeline: normalize in the first stateless stage of the ingest farm (before enrichment). Implement rule set as table-driven maps to allow hotfixes without redeploying code.
- Edge harvester: convert binary blobs (audit buffers) to JSON with conservative default mappings and attach collector provenance tag so downstream can apply specialized fixes.

SIEM export mapping (Elastic / Splunk / QRadar):
- Build an export matrix that translates canonical fields to target SIEM field names. Keep the mapping in a config repo consumed by the exporter service. Example mapping (Elastic):
  - event_type => event.action
  - timestamp_iso8601 => @timestamp
  - request_id => event.request_id
  - actor_id => user.id
  - actor_identity => user.name
  - actor_roles => user.roles
  - outcome => event.outcome
  - outcome_code => event.code
  - resource => resource.name
  - resource_namespace => resource.namespace
  - evidence_refs => file.reference_url
  - provenance => observer.type

- For Splunk, use the same canonical names but add a lightweight transform rule in the forwarder to rename fields. For QRadar, ensure event.source and event.custom_event_id are set so QRadar rules can categorize.

Sampling, retention, and cost tradeoffs:
- Not all artifact payloads can be forwarded in full. Policy:
  - Always keep full artifacts for admin-level events (privilege changes, key management ops) for 90 days in cold storage.
  - For high-volume telemetry (inference token-level logs), sample 1% by default, tagged with sampling_ratio and sampled_policy id. Increase sampling when anomalies detected.
  - Provide dynamic sampling controls surfaced in Redwood Console (per-model / per-route sampling override).

RBAC v2 enforcement & provenance concerns:
- Canonical record must include actor_roles and actor_role_sources. Do NOT attempt to infer roles server-side (this causes drift). If a collector cannot produce roles, tag actor_roles=unknown_role_source and link to which service emitted the doc.
- For impersonation, preserve full chain. Do not collapse chain unless explicitly redacted by policy.

Transformation examples (realistic snippets):
1) Raw sidecar event:
{
  "ts": 1676000000,
  "uid": "u_123",
  "email": "alice@example.com",
  "action": "gen",
  "model": "redwood-4x",
  "req": "r_987",
  "cache": 1
}
Normalized canonical event (after transform):
{
  "event_type": "api_call",
  "timestamp_iso8601": "2023-02-10T12:33:20.000Z",
  "request_id": "r_987",
  "actor_id": "u_123",
  "actor_identity": "alice@example.com",
  "operation": "generate",
  "resource": "model:redwood-4x",
  "kvm_cache_hit": "true",
  "provenance": "sidecar_v2"
}

Operational runbook (triage and validation):
1) Validation checks on ingest (stateless): schema version exists and timestamp within clock skew threshold. If invalid, route to quarantine topic with original payload preserved and emit a metric (evidence.ingest.invalid).
2) Enrichment: if roles present, validate against RBAC service API (async validation). Missing: label event.role_validation=pending.
3) Export: exporter reads canonical records, batches by destination, and applies SIEM mapping table. Export errors are retried with exponential backoff.
4) Failure modes and playbook:
   - Missing request_id: tag event.request_id=generated:<uuid> and mark event for audit review. If more than 0.1% generated ids across an hour for a service, create alert.
   - Role deserialization error: increment evidence.ingest.role_deserialize_error and send sample to forensic queue.
   - SIEM mapping mismatch: exporter should attach original canonical event as compressed attachment to the error log for developers.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests: mapping table unit tests for every mapping in exporter repo.
- Integration tests: end-to-end harness that runs sample collectors -> normalizer -> enrichment -> exporter -> Elastic local cluster. Tests verify queryability of actor_roles and impersonation chain and confirm no truncation.
- Canary rollout: enable normalizer for 5% of production traffic in a dedicated ingest shard. Monitor metrics: ingest.invalid, role_validation.pending, export.fail_rate.
- Migration: maintain an archived mapping layer for older collector versions for 12 months. Run weekly reconciliation jobs comparing counts of canonical events per operation between new and legacy paths.

Open questions / decisions required (short):
- Do we require collector-side signing of artifacts before export for chain-of-custody? (Security prefers yes; ops wary of perf impact.)
- How do we grant SIEM teams read-only access to canonical object store while preserving PII redaction policies?
- Should we make actor_roles a structured array (preferred) or keep it as comma-separated list for simplicity in some SIEMs?

Action items and owners:
- Design adapter for sidecar normalizer: Diego Morales (due 2025-03-15)
- Exporter mapping table repo and CI: Priya Nair (due 2025-03-08)
- RBAC v2 role serialization spec update: Samir Patel (due 2025-03-01)

Appendix A: quick CLI snippets (developer debugging)
- Send a sample raw event to normalization lambda: 
  curl -X POST http://ingest.local/normalize -d @sample_event.json -H "Content-Type: application/json"
- Query canonical events for an actor in local ES: 
  curl 'http://localhost:9200/_search' -d '{"query":{"term":{"actor_identity":"alice@example.com"}}}'

Appendix B: example SIEM mapping config (YAML-like pseudo)
- destination: elastic-prod
  mappings:
    event_type: event.action
    timestamp_iso8601: '@timestamp'
    request_id: event.request_id
    actor_identity: user.name
    actor_roles: user.roles
    provenance: observer.type

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: prefer preserving information over aggressive normalization. If a field is ambiguous, tag with provenance so downstream analysts can trace back to the collector version.
- Please call out any SIEM-specific constraints your team knows (Splunk indexing limits, QRadar custom property size limits) so we can add per-exporter adapters.

History and signals:
- Drafted from recent postmortem JIRA-SEC-4472 and meetings with Observability and SRE. Prior art: collector-forwarder-concordance-protocol, evidence-harvest-orchestrator-proposal. This document attempts to tie those designs into a pragmatic canonical schema and operational runbook.
